items.title: Bob Rosengarden interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, October 6, 1996
items.q: like Buddy Tate, they all mentioned that when they were coming up, everyone was striving for an individual sound.

ctx.x: He’s a piece of work. He’s one of the last of the Mohicans. He plays like Kenny Davern. No one else. He doesn’t play like Pee Wee Russell. He can imitate. He doesn’t play like Benny Goodman or Artie Shaw or anybody else. He plays like Kenny Davern. One of a kind. He really is. And I love to play with him because his time is so good. You can go away and come back three days later and the beat is right exactly where it’s supposed to be.

You know a lot of the gentlemen that we’ve talked to that are in their eighties and so forth, like Buddy Tate, they all mentioned that when they were coming up, everyone was striving for an individual sound.
